main_text.p: modo suam ipsius ira placaverit. Quid quod Iesa. 59. verf. 16. 17. sic legamus: QUUM ITAQUE DEUS VIDIT NUL-LUM ESSE VIRUM, ET OBSTUPUIT NULLUM ESSE INTERVENTOREM (id est) hominem ullum pium, qui pos-set intercedere ad servandam Eccle-siam, nisi idem fuisset Deus) SALUTEM [?]tulit ei (nimirum viro, qui neq; seipsum poterat sistere coram Deo, neq; pro alte-ro intercedere, sed jam erat in peccatis mortuus, Eph. 2. 1.) BRACHIUM IPSIUS (id est, Christum Dei potentiam & sapientiam, 1 Cor. 1. 24.) ET JUSTITIA IPSIUS (idem Christus, qui factus est nobis a Deo sapientia, & justitia, sanctificatio & redemtio, 1 Cor. 1. 30.) hac FULCIVIT eum. Nam (ipse Christus intervē-tor noster Regnū Satanæ potestatem-que tenebrarū debellaturus) INDUIT JUSTITIAM QUASI LORICAM (ut ad Eph. 6. 14. 17.) ET GALEAM SALUTIS CAPITI SUO: INDUIT INQUAM, VES-TIUM ULTIONIS INDUMENTUM, ET AMICIVIT SE ZELO QUASI PALLIO, Sed satis sit, cum semel rationi infanti-enti nunquā alias satisfiat.

page.notes: The running head "ff." is doubtful, possibly "II." or another numeral. Line ends at the right edge are partly cut off by the scan; words there were read from their clipped letters. "SALUTEM ... tulit ei" has an uncertain italic word in the printed "sulit ei" form. Long s has been normalised to s; "Iesa" and "sanctificatio" are as printed. The text is a single paragraph continuing from the previous page, with no paragraph break on this page.
